related_questions.question: How long do COVID vaccine side effects last?
related_questions.snippet: Side effects generally go away in a few days and tend to be mild and temporary, like those experienced after routine vaccinations. Even if you don't experience any side effects, your body is building protection against the virus that causes COVID-19.
related_questions.title: Getting Your COVID-19 Vaccine - CDC

related_questions.question: Can you take ibuprofen after a COVID vaccine?
related_questions.snippet: You may be instructed by the vaccine provider that you can take an antihistamine or acetaminophen or another OTC medicine such as ibuprofen or aspirin to help relieve any vaccine side effects. Or, talk with your provider about taking OTC medicine if you are not sure.
related_questions.title: COVID-19 vaccines - what to expect: MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

related_questions.question: How do you feel after a COVID and flu shot?
related_questions.snippet: Side effects vary from person to person. The most common side effects of a COVID vaccine are a sore arm and sometimes fever, chills, tiredness and headaches for a day or two. Common side effects after a flu shot include soreness, redness and/or swelling where the shot was given.
